title: She moved to the US at 11. Now she runs a $12 billion biotech company.
sources: Carnegie Corporation of New York - Great Immigrants 2026, Reshma Kewalramani profile
Boston University - Vertex CEO and President Reshma Kewalramani feature, 2026
caption:
Reshma Kewalramani was born in Bombay and moved to the US at age 11. In 2020, she became the first woman to lead a large public biotech company.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals posted $12.0 billion in revenue in 2025 under her leadership, up 9% year-over-year. Under Kewalramani, Vertex developed the first FDA-approved CRISPR gene-editing treatment for sickle cell disease.

In 2026, Carnegie Corporation named her to its Great Immigrants list. A path that started as an 11-year-old arriving in a new country now runs one of the treatments changing how a genetic disease gets treated at all.

Sources: Carnegie Corporation, Boston University (2026)
